acuteOverview.title: Overview
acuteOverview.takeaway: Shelfwise manages stock and reservations, structured into six functional code groups.

acuteOverview.title: Dependency rules
acuteOverview.takeaway: Three rules ensure a readable, decoupled, and testable system structure.

acuteOverview.title: API and orchestration
acuteOverview.takeaway: API handlers delegate to a reservation orchestrator that manages atomic stock reservations with a timeout.

acuteOverview.title: Domain services
acuteOverview.takeaway: Two independent domain services manage stock and pricing with strict dependencies.

acuteOverview.title: Supplier integration
acuteOverview.takeaway: Supplier feed adapter fetches, transforms, and records deliveries, logging unparsable data.

acuteOverview.title: Persistence and external systems
acuteOverview.takeaway: Key systems for persistence and external interactions are defined.

acuteOverview.title: Observability and error handling
acuteOverview.takeaway: Structured logging and a specific retry policy handle API failures.

acuteOverview.takeaway: The admin web UI is for warehouse staff, uses a REST API, and has no direct DB access.

acuteOverview.title: Where to start reading

acuteOverview.title: Known gaps
acuteOverview.takeaway: Critical gaps exist in admin UI testing, stock consistency, and dead-letter alerts.

ai.stableNodeKey: (outline) § subtitle#0

content.text: Shelfwise is a service responsible for tracking warehouse stock and managing reservations for incoming orders.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#0

content.text: It is a deployable TypeScript service with a small admin frontend.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#1

content.text: At its peak, Shelfwise processes approximately 3,000 reservations per hour.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#2

content.text: This tour organizes the code by responsibility, detailing module ownership, key files, and inter-group dependencies.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#3

content.text: The code is divided into the following groups: presentation, API and orchestration, domain services, supplier integration, persistence and external systems, and observability and error handling.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#4

content.text: This section introduces the Shelfwise service, its technical characteristics, performance, and the organizational structure of its codebase for a guided tour.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Overview § text#5

snapshot.content: Domain modules independent of HTTP layer

content.text: Domain modules (ledger, pricing rules) must not depend on the HTTP layer, ensuring they are usable in non-web contexts like scripts or tests.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#0

snapshot.content: Ledger is the sole writer to Postgres for stock

content.text: Only the ledger module is permitted to write stock data to Postgres. Other modules, such as the orchestrator and adapter, must interact with Postgres for stock updates through the ledger.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#1

snapshot.content: Supplier feed adapter exclusively calls supplier API

content.text: The supplier feed adapter is the only component allowed to make calls to the supplier API.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#2

content.text: These rules enforce a clear separation of concerns and maintain a structured architecture. They prevent tight coupling.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#3

content.text: Three rules keep the structure readable.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Dependency rules § text#4

content.text: HTTP handlers in
src/api/routes.ts
are the sole entry point for requests. They validate the request body, attach a correlation ID, and delegate tasks without implementing business rules.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#0

content.text: The reservation orchestrator in
src/orders/reserve.ts
manages the entire reservation process, from initiation to completion.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#1

content.text: The orchestrator requests stock reservation from the stock ledger and pricing information from pricing rules. Upon successful completion of both, it publishes a
StockReserved
event to the message broker.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#2

content.text: If the stock ledger cannot reserve the full quantity, the orchestrator rejects the entire order; partial reservations are not allowed.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#3

content.text: Reservations not confirmed within 15 minutes are automatically released by the ledger, making the stock available again.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#4

content.text: The API acts as a thin layer, delegating all business logic to the reservation orchestrator. The orchestrator ensures atomic reservations, either reserving the full quantity or rejecting the entire order. A time-based release mechanism prevents indefinite stock holding for unconfirmed reservations.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › API and orchestration § text#5

content.text: The
src/ledger/ledger.ts
module:
Manages stock levels.
Records all changes (reserve, release, restock) as append-only ledger entries.
Writes entries to Postgres.
Is the
only
module permitted to write to stock tables; other modules must request changes through it.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#0

content.text: The
src/pricing/rules.ts
module:
Calculates order prices based on supplier price lists and active discounts.
Reads price lists from Redis, where they are cached for 300 seconds.
Does not modify stock levels.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#1

content.text: Domain modules:
Do not import anything from
src/api/
or
src/orders/
Follow an inward dependency rule: API calls orchestrator, orchestrator calls domain modules.
Depend solely on persistence and platform helpers.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#2

content.text: The two domain services, stock ledger and pricing rules, are independent and have clearly defined responsibilities. They enforce strict boundaries on data access and dependencies.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Domain services § text#3

content.text: The supplier feed adapter is located at
src/suppliers/feedAdapter.ts
and is responsible for ingesting restock information from suppliers.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#0

content.text: The adapter calls the supplier API every 10 minutes to fetch new delivery data.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#1

content.text: Each delivery received from the supplier API is converted into a restock record.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#2

content.text: The converted restock is then sent to the stock ledger for recording.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#3

content.text: The adapter encapsulates knowledge of the supplier's data format, ensuring that any changes on the supplier's side are isolated to this single file.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#4

content.text: If the adapter cannot parse a delivery, it logs the error and skips the delivery. There are no retries for unparsable data, as repeated attempts would yield the same failure.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#5

content.text: The supplier integration process is a scheduled task that fetches, transforms, and records supplier deliveries. It handles parsing errors by logging and skipping, without retries.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#6

content.text: The process explicitly logs and skips unparsable deliveries, preventing infinite retries of bad data. This ensures system stability but means unparsable deliveries are not processed.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Supplier integration § text#7

content.text: Stores ledger entries and current stock levels.
Is the definitive source for stock information.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#3

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Persistence and external systems § text#4

content.text: All modules use
src/platform/log.ts
for logging.
Each event is logged as a single JSON line.
Every log entry includes a correlation ID, added by HTTP handlers.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#0

content.text: HTTP handlers log each request.
The retry helper logs every failed attempt.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#1

content.text: The feed adapter uses
src/platform/retry.ts
for supplier API calls due to potential failures.
The retry policy includes:
A maximum of 5 attempts per delivery.
Exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds, doubling with each failure, and capped at 60 seconds.
After the 5th failed attempt, the delivery is published to the
inventory.dlq
dead-letter queue on the message broker for staff review in the admin UI.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Observability and error handling § text#2

content.text: Retries are only for supplier calls.
Reservations are never automatically retried; failed reservations return an error to the caller.

Looking up stock levels

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#0

content.text: The reservation orchestrator and feed adapter can simultaneously modify product stock. The ledger uses a database row lock for consistency, but its effectiveness under peak load is unmeasured.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#1

content.text: Dead-lettered deliveries are only discovered when the admin UI is manually checked. There is no alert mechanism for when the
inventory.dlq
begins to accumulate messages.

ai.stableNodeKey: Shelfwise inventory service: a tour of the codebase › Known gaps § text#2

content.text: Key gaps include a lack of automated tests for the admin UI, unmeasured stock consistency under peak load, and the absence of alerts for dead-lettered deliveries.
